entries.proposition: The immunosuppressed arm is three high-dose animals given mycophenolate mofetil plus rapamycin, within the 90-day cohort.
entries.snippet: Three HD subjects from the 90-day cohort also received immunosuppression (IS) consisting of mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) and rapamycin

entries.proposition: MMF was withdrawn on day 60 (earlier in one animal), rapamycin continued; the regimen began three weeks before dosing.
entries.snippet: Rapamycin was used for the entirety of the study, whereas MMF was stopped on study day 60.

entries.proposition: The immunosuppression regimen itself caused diarrhoea, anorexia, weight loss and anaemia, starting before vector dosing.
entries.snippet: The IS regimen administered to three animals caused adverse effects of decreased appetite, diarrhea, and weight loss that all started prior to test article administration.

entries.proposition: Sensory-neuron cell-body degeneration with mononuclear infiltrate was seen in at least one DRG of every animal sampled except one immunosuppressed animal.
entries.snippet: in at least one DRG and trigeminal nerve ganglia of all animals except one HD IS animal

entries.proposition: The text says incidence and severity trended lower with immunosuppression.
entries.snippet: Overall, the incidence and severity of the DRG degeneration and axonopathy trended toward lower scores in the HD IS animals (Figure 3G).

entries.proposition: Figure 3G: DRG cumulative score is about 2.7 (high dose), about 2.0 (high dose with immunosuppression) and about 2.3 (low dose), with overlapping error bars at three animals per group; axonopathy score is about 5.0 and 4.7 (high dose, day 90 and 180), about 2.4 (with immunosuppression) and about 4.4 (low dose), vehicle and day-14 zero.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3G bar charts, read at native resolution: DRG cumulative score bars Vehicle 0, HD D90 about 2.7, HD+IS D90 about 2.0, LD D90 about 2.3; axonopathy cumulative score Vehicle 0, HD D14 0, HD D90 about 5, HD D180 about 4.7, HD+IS D90 about 2.4, LD D90 about 4.4; error bars (SD) overlap in the DRG panel; individual animals plotted as symbols.

entries.proposition: The authors state the DRG and axonopathy findings and the transgene-directed lymphocyte clustering were present in animals whose T-cell responses were pharmacologically suppressed.
entries.snippet: However, these findings were still present in animals with pharmacologically suppressed T cell responses.

entries.proposition: The authors say immunosuppression may help but no definitive conclusion can be drawn because of cohort size.
entries.snippet: it is hard to draw any definitive conclusions due to study limitations, such as cohort size

entries.proposition: Vector genome levels in the high-dose group were about tenfold higher than in the low-dose group.
entries.snippet: found that levels in the HD group were approximately 10 times higher than the LD group

entries.proposition: The authors state no histological lesions were seen in vehicle-treated or day-14 vector-treated animals.
entries.snippet: no histological lesions in vehicle-treated or day 14 vector-treated animals

entries.proposition: The authors suggest immune responses may worsen rather than cause an initial injury, citing overexpression toxicity with a strong promoter.
entries.snippet: Perhaps immune responses are not causative but worsen an initial injury

entries.proposition: The authors report no clinical consequence of the sensory lesions and no rodent precedent.
entries.snippet: To the best of our knowledge, no published reports exist of similar DRG toxicity in mice or rats dosed intrathecally with various AAV vectors.

entries.proposition: The IS animals alone showed a day-60 anaemia and a minimal ALT rise in one animal that resolved; no transaminase change was found in non-IS animals.
entries.snippet: we did not find any significant abnormalities in the CBC, blood chemistry (including transaminases), or coagulation parameters
